definitions.explanation: Sexual passion or carnal desire, often carrying a literary or somewhat clinical tone.

examples.japanese: {色情|しきじょう}に{溺|おぼ}れる。
その{小説|しょうせつ}は{色情|しきじょう}をテーマにしている。
examples.english: That novel has sensuality as its theme.

examples.japanese: {仏教|ぶっきょう}では{色情|しきじょう}は{煩悩|ぼんのう}の{一|ひと}つとされ、{悟|さと}りの{妨|さまた}げになると{教|おし}えられる。
examples.english: In Buddhism, lust is considered one of the worldly desires and is taught to be an obstacle to enlightenment.

notes:
Composed of {色|しき} (sensual desire; color) + {情|じょう} (emotion; passion). The kanji {色|しき} has long carried sexual connotations in Japanese, as in {色恋|いろこい} (love affair) and {好色|こうしょく} (lustful). {色情|しきじょう} is a literary or formal word; everyday speech uses {性欲|せいよく} instead.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {色情|しきじょう}に{溺|おぼ}れる: to be consumed by lust
- {色情|しきじょう}{狂|きょう}: sexual mania; nymphomania
- {色情|しきじょう}{的|てき}: sensual; erotic

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {性欲|せいよく}: sexual desire — the standard modern term; more neutral and direct than the literary {色情|しきじょう}
- {情欲|じょうよく}: passion; carnal desire — similar register to {色情|しきじょう}, also somewhat literary
- {好色|こうしょく}: lustfulness; lechery — describes the tendency or character of being lustful, rather than the desire itself
